'''Kevin Mark Buzzard''' (born 21 September 1968) is a British [[mathematician]] and currently a professor of pure mathematics at [[Imperial College London]]. He specialises in [[arithmetic geometry]] and the [[Langlands program]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Buzzard |first=Kevin |title=What is the Xena project? |url=https://xenaproject.wordpress.com/what-is-the-xena-project/ |access-date=1 July 2022 |website=Xena Project|date=8 May 2019 }}</ref>

==Biography==
While attending the [[Royal Grammar School, High Wycombe]] he competed in the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]], where he won a bronze medal in 1986 and a gold medal with a perfect score in 1987.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.imo-official.org/participant_r.aspx?id=10962|title=Kevin Mark Buzzard|work=Participants|publisher=International Mathematical Olympiad|access-date=2024-04-01}}</ref>

He obtained a B.A. degree in Mathematics at [[Trinity College, Cambridge]], where he was [[Senior Wrangler]] in 1990, and a [[Certificate of Advanced Study in Mathematics|C.A.S.M.]] in 1991.<ref name="cv"/> He then received his Ph.D. under the supervision of [[Richard Taylor (mathematician)|Richard Taylor]] with a thesis titled ''The levels of modular representations'' in 1995.<ref name="cv"/><ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=49405}}</ref>

He took a lectureship at [[Imperial College London]] in 1998, a readership in 2002, and was appointed to a professorship in 2004. From October to December 2002 he held a visiting professorship at [[Harvard University]], having previously worked at the [[Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton]] (1995), the [[University of California Berkeley]] (1996-7), and the [[Institute Henri Poincaré]] in Paris (2000).<ref name="cv">{{cite web |url=http://www.ma.ic.ac.uk/~buzzard/stuff/cv.pdf |title=Curriculum Vitae |website=Kevin Buzzard |date=8 November 2012 |access-date=14 February 2024}}</ref>

He was awarded a Whitehead Prize by the [[London Mathematical Society]] in 2002 for "his distinguished work in number theory",<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.lms.ac.uk/activities/prizes_com/citations02/KMBUZZARD.html|title=Citation for Kevin Mark Buzzard|access-date=2007-02-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091003221540/http://www.lms.ac.uk/activities/prizes_com/citations02/KMBUZZARD.html|archive-date=2009-10-03|url-status=dead}}</ref> and the [[Berwick Prizes|Senior Berwick Prize]] in 2008.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.lms.ac.uk/activities/prizes_com/pastwinners.html|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070804191203/http://www.lms.ac.uk/activities/prizes_com/pastwinners.html|url-status=dead|title=LMS Prizewinners|archivedate=August 4, 2007}}</ref>

In 2017, he launched an ongoing [[Formal verification|formalization]] project and blog involving the [[Lean theorem prover]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Buzzard |first=Kevin |date=5 September 2019 |title=The future of mathematics? |url=https://www.ma.imperial.ac.uk/~buzzard/one_off_lectures/msr.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210824092439/https://www.ma.imperial.ac.uk/~buzzard/one_off_lectures/msr.pdf |archive-date=24 August 2021 |access-date=1 July 2022}}</ref> and has since promoted the use of computer [[proof assistants]] in future mathematics research. He gave a plenary lecture at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 2022 on the topic.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SEID4XYFN7o&t=237 |title=The rise of formalism in mathematics|website=YouTube|date=9 July 2022|author=Kevin Buzzard}}</ref>

He was the PhD supervisor to musician [[Dan Snaith]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ma.imperial.ac.uk/~buzzard/maths/research/notes|title=Kevin Buzzard's research notes|access-date=16 July 2022}}</ref> also known as Caribou, who received a PhD in mathematics from [[Imperial College London]] for his work on ''[[Siegel modular form|Overconvergent Siegel Modular Symbols]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ma.imperial.ac.uk/~buzzard/maths/research/notes/sp2n.pdf|title=Overconvergent Siegel Modular Symbols|author=Daniel Snaith|website=2.imperial.acuk|access-date=16 July 2022}}</ref>

In 2024, Buzzard and collaborators were awarded a five-year [[Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council|EPSRC]] grant to begin formalising [[Fermat's Last Theorem]] in Lean.<ref>{{Cite web |title=EP/Y022904/1: 'Formalising Fermat' |url=https://gow.epsrc.ukri.org/NGBOViewGrant.aspx?GrantRef=EP/Y022904/1 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240726143703/https://gow.epsrc.ukri.org/NGBOViewGrant.aspx?GrantRef=EP/Y022904/1 |archive-date=2024-07-26 |access-date= |website=ESPRC}}</ref>
